JDK, JRE, and JVM

Stage 1 Concept ⏱ 15 min 📖 Glossary

Three letters, one pipeline: the JDK builds, the JRE runs, the JVM executes. Install the JDK and you quietly get all three.

🔎 Motivating questionOn a film set, who writes the script, who owns the studio, and who actually acts?

Objectives

  • Tell JDK, JRE, JVM apart
  • Trace .java to running app
  • Pick what to install

Needs first: What Is Java and What Can It Build?

1 Start with an analogy

Real life first, code second.

Script tools (JDK) → equipped studio (JRE) → actor (JVM) performing your scene. The writer needs the studio; the audience only needs the studio + actor.

⚠️ Where the analogy breaksWhere it breaks: real studios differ per film. JVMs are deliberately near-identical — the same bytecode behaves the same on every system. That sameness is the product.

2 The concept, plainly

One idea at a time, words before jargon.

The JVM (Java Virtual Machine) executes bytecode and manages memory. There is one per platform, all behaving the same.

The JRE (Runtime Environment) is JVM + the standard libraries needed to run apps — for users, no compiler inside.

The JDK (Development Kit) is JRE + the javac compiler + tools like java and jar — for developers. Install a JDK 17 and you cover everything.

Your daily loop: javac translates .java → .class; java launches the JVM on that class. An error at the first step is a code problem; at the second, a runtime problem.

⚙️ Tech details — precise facts
  • javac exists only in the JDK. If your terminal says “javac not found”, you installed a JRE (or nothing), not a JDK.
  • java -version and javac -version should both report 17 — mismatched pairs cause confusing errors.
  • Free JDK 17 builds: Temurin (Eclipse), Oracle OpenJDK, Amazon Corretto — all run this course identically.

3 Watch it move: JDK contains JRE contains JVM

Step at your pace. Text explains every move.

4 Live code demo

Small, correct Java 17 (LTS) code. Read, trace, copy.

terminalshell
$ javac Main.java   # JDK: source -> Main.class
$ java Main         # JRE/JVM: run it, prints Hi
Hi
▶ Output Hi
  • javac only exists in the JDK — it compiles.
  • java launches using the JRE + JVM — it runs.
  • First line builds; second line executes.
💻 Terminal commandsType these lines in your terminal, not in a Java file.
💡 Why this output?Compile once with the JDK; then any machine’s JVM executes the bytecode. Two tools, two jobs.

6 Common mistakes (at least 3)

Wrong, why, fixed — learn from realistic slips.

❌ Mistake 1: Installing only the JRE to learn coding.Why: A JRE cannot compile anything — you will stare at “javac not found”.
✅ Fix: Install a JDK 17 (Temurin or Oracle) instead.
❌ Mistake 2: “The JVM is the compiler.”Why: javac compiles; the JVM runs. Swapping the words guarantees confusion later.
✅ Fix: javac = build, java = run.
❌ Mistake 3: Mixing a Java 8 javac with a Java 17 java (or reverse).Why: Old builders + new runners (or reverse) produce bizarre version errors.
✅ Fix: Check java -version and javac -version: both should say 17.

7 Guided practice

Hints first, solutions only after a real try.

Who does what?

Match each to its job: A) javac B) java C) JVM — compiles / launches / executes.

HintBuild → launch → execute.
SolutionA compiles source, B launches the runtime, C executes bytecode.
Which package for whom?

You want to WRITE Java. Your friend only wants to RUN your app. What does each install?

HintCoders need the compiler; players need the player.
SolutionYou: JDK. Friend: JRE (a JDK works too, just heavier).

8 Lesson quiz

3+ questions. Attempts saved locally; review queue learns your weak spots.

9 Takeaways + next step

  • JVM runs, JRE runs-with-libraries, JDK builds.
  • Install JDK 17; both version commands should say 17.
  • javac builds; java runs. Errors tell you which stage broke.
🧠 Recall challengeWhat does each letter-group give you that the smaller one does not?
✏️ Do on your ownRun java -version and javac -version in a terminal and write down both numbers.
